=== FINDING 1 (BLOCKING FOR MERGE, NOT A DEFECT IN THIS DIFF): every Dependabot PR in this repository is structurally unmergeable ===
CI is RED on this PR. I established exactly which steps are red and why, rather than assuming the diff caused it. Across all six `test` jobs the failing steps are precisely three, and all three fail for a reason tied to the AUTHOR being Dependabot, not to the one line that changed:

(1) `lwb-env-leak` and (2) `lwb-env-leak-history`. Both read `${{ secrets.LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES }}`. A Dependabot-triggered workflow run does not receive the repository's ACTIONS secrets; it receives the repository's DEPENDABOT secrets. MEASURED: `gh api repos/LEAPWare-Software/LEAPWare-BuildCraft/dependabot/secrets` returns `{"total_count":0,"secrets":[]}`. So on these runs the expression expands to the empty string. REPRODUCED LOCALLY at this head: `LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES="" python scripts/lwb_check_env_leak.py` -> exit 1, `FAIL: lwb-env-leak UNCONFIGURED: LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES is unset or empty, so no real private name was scanned for and a clean result proves nothing.`
    This is the fail-closed design WORKING. It is the good shape: 'I could not check' is not reporting as 'I checked and found nothing'. The defect is not in the check; it is that the gate's input never reaches it on a bot PR, so the failure is permanent and no push to this branch can clear it.
    I verified the failure is NOT a concealed real leak, in both directions: with needles configured the tree and the base..head range are clean (above), AND the gate is not vacuous -- I planted a synthetic needle string into docs/architecture.md and it failed with `FAIL: docs/architecture.md:136: private-project name leak (needle #1)`, naming file and line, then restored the file. (The needle itself is deliberately not reproduced anywhere in this record -- see near-miss 2.)
    REMEDY IS REPO-SIDE, NOT PR-SIDE: add `LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES` as a **Dependabot** secret (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Dependabot), or give these two steps an explicit, loudly-announced bot-author exemption. Nothing a reviewer or an author can push to this branch fixes it.

(3) `lwb-proof-pr`. REPRODUCED LOCALLY: `FAIL: PR #61 carries no proof/*.json record for itself.` Dependabot does not write proof records and cannot be taught to. Owner directive 7 applies to every PR, so this step is also permanently red for any bot-authored PR.

CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly because it is the actionable part: auto-queue.yml lands a PR only when EVERY required check is green (its own header comment says readiness is exactly that). With three permanently-red steps, no Dependabot PR in this repository can ever be auto-queued, and #2/#3/#4 having been 'spent unattended' (reviews/README.md, BOOTSTRAP_EXEMPT_PRS) suggests this has been true for a while. Landing this bump requires either the Dependabot-secret fix above plus a proof record, or re-cutting the one-line change as an LWB-agent-authored PR.

=== NEAR-MISS 1, CAUGHT AND PRINTED RATHER THAN HIDDEN ===
I came within one command of filing a critical finding that the `lwb-lanes` CI step omits `--pr-number`, which -- since `main()` defaults it to 0 and `check_lanes()` returns `[]` immediately on 0 -- would have meant the entire shared-path independent-review gate never ran in CI while reporting green, i.e. that the reason this reviewer routine exists is vacuous. It is MY artifact, not the repo's: I had read the step through `grep -A 14`, whose window ended exactly one line above `--pr-number ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}`. Printing `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 198-206 verbatim shows the argument is present and correct. NO FINDING. (Separately and correctly: running the script without `--pr-number` does print `lwb-lanes check skipped (not running under a PR)` and exit 0, which is the documented, intended behaviour for a push to main after merge.)
I opened a finding titled 'checkout v5+ may flip the persist-credentials default and break a later git push in this workflow', then read auto-queue.yml end to end before filing it. The job performs no git write at all: it reads scripts/cloud/auto_queue.py out of the checkout and passes a token to it through an explicit `GH_TOKEN:` env key (`secrets.AUTO_TOKEN_QUEUE`), never through git's persisted credentials. No step depends on what checkout leaves in .git/config. Finding withdrawn before it was written down as one; recorded here because a withdrawn suspicion a reviewer hides is worth less than one it prints.

Running `lwb_check_env_leak.py --range` over my own staged record commit failed: `reviews/61/cloud-reviewer-b.json:10: private-project name leak (needle #1)`.   MY FIRST ATTEMPT WAS REJECTED, AND THE REJECTION IS ITSELF FINDING 4. I first wrote `dependabot-bot-github-actions-49699333-2026-09-24`, putting the real GitHub user id in the token position. `scripts/lwb_lanes.py` rejected it: `commit_author_id ...: session-token must not itself be date-shaped`. Traced to `_DATE_SHAPED_RE = ^\d{4}-?\d{2}-?\d{2}$`, which is meant to catch a compact `YYYYMMDD` token but matches ANY 8-digit string -- and `49699333` is 8 digits. So the validator rejects a legitimate, real, unambiguous identifier for being numeric and the wrong length. This is exactly the falsification pressure `reviews/README.md` says the right-to-left parse exists to remove, just relocated: the validator's reward for using a true identifier is a red gate, and its reward for inventing a fake one is green. I did not relabel my way around it by padding or mangling the number -- I moved the user id into the role-and-model part, where it is still stated truthfully, and used the commit's own sha as the token. Suggested repo-side fix: tighten `_DATE_SHAPED_RE` to plausible dates (e.g. require a leading `19`/`20` and month <= 12) so a bare numeric id is not mistaken for one.
- `commit_author_agent`: FORCED AND FALSE, see finding 3. The schema enum offers claude|codex|human and the author is a bot. I chose `human` because its meaning inside `check_lanes` -- 'not lane-bound, unrestricted' -- is the least wrong of the three for a commit outside the lane system, NOT because it is true. Flagging it here is the honest handling; silently picking it would not be.
